status_note: Drafted from the abstracts by the AI assistant on 2026-11-24. Must be checked and confirmed by a person before results are reported as accuracy. Change status to 'confirmed' and fill confirmed_by when done.

schoenfeld2017volume.evidence: The findings indicate a graded dose-response relationship whereby increases in RT volume produce greater gains in muscle hypertrophy.

schoenfeld2019volume.evidence: muscle hypertrophy follows a dose-response relationship, with increasingly greater gains achieved with higher training volumes.

heaselgrave2019.evidence: There were no significant differences between groups in MT or indices of strength. However, effect-size estimates revealed that the magnitude of response was "moderate to large" for MOD and HIGH.
heaselgrave2019.note: Genuinely ambiguous: non-significant differences but moderate-to-large effect sizes. Any cautious reading is accepted; 'positive' is not.

schoenfeld2016frequency.evidence: frequencies of training twice a week promote superior hypertrophic outcomes to once a week.

schoenfeld2019frequency.evidence: resistance training frequency does not significantly or meaningfully impact muscle hypertrophy when volume is equated.

campos2002.evidence: the low to intermediate repetition resistance-training programs induced a greater hypertrophic effect compared to the high repetition regimen.
campos2002.note: Fewer repetitions maximum means a heavier load, so hypertrophy increases with load.

mitchell2012.evidence: a lower load lifted to failure resulted in similar hypertrophy as a heavy load lifted to failure.

schoenfeld2016rest.evidence: longer rest periods promote greater increases in muscle strength and hypertrophy in young resistance-trained men.

ahtiainen2005.evidence: both 3-month training periods performed with either the longer or the shorter rest periods between the sets resulted in similar gains in muscle mass and strength.

morton2018.evidence: Dietary protein supplementation significantly enhanced changes in muscle strength and size during prolonged RET in healthy adults.

erskine2012.evidence: protein supplementation did not augment elbow flexor muscle strength and size changes that occurred after 12 wk of RT.
